clue.text: Two dears getting sozzled imbibing a drink

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so the scrambled letters take in the A
sozzled means very drunk, so the letters of the words before it stagger into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Two darlings get tipsy while sipping a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange TWO and DEARS ('getting sozzled') to SODWATER, then let it take in A ('imbibing'), giving the fizzy mixer.
explanation.definitionFit: Soda water is carbonated water, a drink often used as a mixer.

clue.text: Some marvellous entertainment making one ecstatic

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A wonderful show leaves the audience in raptures.
explanation.definitionFit: Sent is a dated slang adjective for thrilled or transported with delight, as in a performance that sent you.

clue.text: Various folk plunging into the depths with energy

parts.note: people who plunge into deep water are divers
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A mixed group of people dive into deep water, full of vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: Diverse and various are synonyms, both meaning of many differing kinds.

clue.text: Short day for getting married

indicators.note: short says the day's name is cut down, keeping only its opening letters

parts.note: Wednesday is a day of the week

explanation.surface: A brief day set aside for a wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: WED is the usual abbreviation for Wednesday, here reached by cutting the day's name short.
explanation.definitionFit: To wed is to marry, and wed as a participle describes a couple being married.

clue.text: Number given to worker who lives in another's house?

parts.note: ten is a number
the worker ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: A labourer is given a house number, asking who lives in someone else's property.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenant rents and occupies property owned by a landlord, so the home belongs to someone else.

clue.text: People finding fault with agent — a football team?

parts.note: a rep, short for representative, acts as an agent for a firm
Rovers is a common British football club name, such as Blackburn Rovers or Bristol Rovers

explanation.surface: Critics carp about a sports agent and wonder whether he is a football team.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who reproves rebukes or scolds others, so reprovers are critics who find fault.

clue.text: Noise of dog cut short in saloon?

indicators.note: cut short says the final letter of the word is lopped off

parts.note: a dog's noise is a bark

explanation.surface: A dog's yap is interrupted in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saloon' looks like a car, but here it is the saloon bar of a British pub, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A saloon is a drinking room in a pub or Wild West town, a bar serving alcohol.

clue.text: Drills black minerals

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
ores are minerals mined for metal

explanation.surface: Machines bore through dark mineral deposits.
explanation.definitionFit: To bore is to make a hole with a drill, so bores is a verb synonym of drills.

clue.text: Model again needing break, see, when upset

parts.note: a rest is a break from work

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city, and a bishop's see is his diocese

explanation.surface: A fashion model needs a break, see, when she is upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' looks like a verb but is a bishop's diocese; ELY, a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, turned upside down gives YLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To restyle is to shape or fashion anew, as with a haircut, which is to model it again.

clue.text: Northern girl and boy from a state in America

parts.note: Eva is a girl's name
Dan is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A northern girl and boy came from an American state.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nevadan is a native or resident of Nevada, a US state, and the word is also an adjective.

clue.text: Father, gentleman going round capital city

parts.note: pa is an informal name for father

indicators.note: going round means turning about, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: sir is the title for a gentleman

explanation.surface: Dad and a gentleman tour a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Paris is the capital of France, one of the best-known capital cities.

clue.text: Extremely desultory men falling apart

indicators.note: falling apart suggests the words collapse and their letters are rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Aimless men are thoroughly going to pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Tremendously is an intensifying adverb, meaning to a very great degree, the same as extremely.

clue.text: Modified statistical figure assessed

parts.note: the mode is the most frequent value in a set of data
to rate is to assess or evaluate

explanation.surface: A statistic has been altered and evaluated.
explanation.definitionFit: Moderated means toned down or adjusted, so a moderated thing has been modified.

clue.text: Fast river receding — see crossing

indicators.note: crossing means stretching across, so the outer word spans the reversed river

parts.note: to spy is to see or catch sight of

indicators.note: receding means going backwards, so the river's name is read in reverse

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland

explanation.surface: A rapid river ebbs while someone watches people crossing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' looks like a mere aside but is the container, a verb meaning to spot; 'crossing' says it straddles the reversed river.
explanation.definitionFit: Speedy and fast are synonyms, both meaning moving quickly.

clue.text: Part of sentence pupils learn about in English at school?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the grammatical ... of a sentence

definitions.text: pupils learn about in English at school?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a school ..., such as English, that pupils study

explanation.walkthrough: English is cleverly both the topic studied and the place where sentence parts are taught, which the question mark flags.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar the subject is the noun phrase doing the verb; at school a subject is a course of study.

clue.text: The French fever in a group of clubs

parts.note: le is French for the
ague is an old word for a malarial fever

explanation.surface: French fever sweeps through some sports clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A league is an association of sports clubs that play against each other in a competition.

clue.text: Terrible danger descending on a country

indicators.note: in a down clue the scrambled letters come down on top of the A
terrible signals the word is wrecked, its letters thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Awful danger falls on a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Grenada is a Caribbean island nation, which is a country.

clue.text: Stone and tree over den, one hidden

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the tree's name sits above what follows

parts.note: the ash is a tree

indicators.note: hidden here means tucked away out of sight, so that letter disappears from the den

parts.note: an animal's den is its lair
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A stone and a tree stand above an animal's den where someone hides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hidden' would normally signal a word lurking in the clue; here it means the I is taken away, leaving LAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashlar is masonry made of large, square-cut blocks of dressed stone.

clue.text: Two figures working together in IT

definitions.note: IT, information technology, is defined by the whole term here; binary is the language of computing

parts.note: binary means relating to two, a base-two scheme
a system is a set of parts, here numbers, working together as a whole

explanation.surface: Two people working as a team in the IT department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'figures' suggests people, but these are numbers; the definition is just IT at the end, with 'in' as the link.
explanation.definitionFit: The binary system, counting with only the digits zero and one, underpins all computing and information technology.

clue.text: Restraint lifted — good for entering that country

indicators.note: entering means going in, so this letter sits inside the reversed word
in a down clue lifted means raised up, so the word reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a rein restrains a horse

explanation.surface: A restriction is lifted, which is good for anyone entering the country.
explanation.walkthrough: REIN read upwards is NIER, and G goes inside it to give NI-G-ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Niger is a landlocked nation in West Africa; 'that country' points back to the 'country' of the neighbouring clue.

clue.text: Boss of half the college's learners?

indicators.note: half the says only the first half of the word is kept

parts.note: learners at college are students

explanation.surface: The head of half the students at a college?
explanation.definitionFit: A stud is an ornamental knob or boss, such as a raised metal stud on a shield or belt.

clue.text: Crew with heaviness, not weak

indicators.note: not means without, so this letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: heaviness is weight

explanation.surface: A crew that is heavy but not feeble.
explanation.walkthrough: An eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen, as in the Boat Race.
explanation.definitionFit: In rowing an eight is a boat crewed by eight rowers, so the word names the crew itself.

clue.text: Criticise innocent person, a saint

parts.note: a lamb is a meek and innocent person

explanation.surface: Attacking a guiltless person who is a saint.
explanation.definitionFit: To lambast is to attack verbally or censure harshly, a strong synonym of criticise.

clue.text: Bishop given honour has this crowd turning up

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A bishop given an honour finds a crowd arriving.
explanation.definitionFit: A mob is a large, disorderly crowd of people.

clue.text: Feature of Dartmoor — rubbish thrown around

indicators.note: thrown around means turned about, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: rot means nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: Litter scattered across a Dartmoor beauty spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A tor is a rocky hilltop outcrop, typical of Dartmoor, a moorland in Devon in south-west England.

clue.text: Quick move by directors — this target will be hit

parts.note: to dart is to make a quick movement
a company's directors form its board

explanation.surface: Company directors make a swift decision, knowing a target will be struck.
explanation.definitionFit: A dartboard is the round target at which darts are thrown in the pub game.
